Ancient Indian history

Major dynasties of ancient India: a table for students

By @archaeologywala for Talaash Heritage · Updated 15 October 2026

The major dynasties of ancient India run from the Haryankas and Nandas of Magadha through the Mauryas, Shungas, Satavahanas, Kushanas and Guptas, to early medieval powers such as the Vardhanas, Chalukyas, Pallavas, Rashtrakutas, Palas, Pratiharas and Cholas. Each is best remembered by its founder, capital, dates and one lasting monument or source.

We run museum gallery studies and replica coin sessions that turn this dynasty table into objects, for schools, colleges and exam aspirants.

How to use this list of ancient Indian dynasties

Dynasty tables are the backbone of exam preparation, but they only stick when each name is tied to a place and an object. For each dynasty below, remember three things: who founded it, where it ruled from, and one thing you could go and see. Dates are approximate and vary a little between textbooks. For the wider sequence of periods, see our Indian history timeline.

North Indian dynasties: Magadha to the Guptas

These dynasties ruled mainly from the Ganga plain and the north-west, from the age of the Mahajanapadas to the end of the Guptas.

Early medieval north and east India

The three-way contest between the Palas, the Gurjara-Pratiharas and the Rashtrakutas for control of Kanauj, in the 8th to 10th centuries, is often called the tripartite struggle.

Seeing the dynasties in their monuments

The fastest way to fix a dynasty in memory is to stand in one of its buildings. In Delhi the National Museum displays coins and sculpture from almost every dynasty here, and a museum morning with an archaeologist can follow them in order. Coins are especially useful because rulers put their names and titles on them; our numismatics session with replicas shows how to read them.

Further afield, the Pattadakal and Aihole sites show Chalukya temples side by side, and Mamallapuram holds Pallava rock-cut and structural work. For individual dynasties, read our guides to the Mauryan empire, the Gupta empire and the Chola dynasty.

Questions people ask

Which was the first dynasty of ancient India?

For the historical period, the Haryanka dynasty of Magadha, founded by Bimbisara in the 6th century BCE, is usually listed first. Earlier ruling lineages are mentioned in Vedic and epic texts, but they cannot be dated or confirmed in the same way.

Which ancient Indian dynasty ruled the longest?

The Western Gangas of Karnataka ruled for several centuries, roughly the 4th to 11th centuries CE, and the Satavahanas for about three to four centuries. Among major imperial dynasties, the imperial Cholas, from about 850 to 1279 CE, had one of the longest runs.

Who founded the Chalukya dynasty of Badami?

Pulakeshin I founded the Chalukya dynasty of Badami (Vatapi) in the mid 6th century CE. His grandson Pulakeshin II is the best-known ruler; the Aihole inscription of 634 CE records his victory over Harsha on the Narmada.

What was the tripartite struggle?

The tripartite struggle was the contest between the Palas of Bengal, the Gurjara-Pratiharas of western India and the Rashtrakutas of the Deccan for control of Kanauj and the Ganga plain, roughly from the late 8th to the 10th century CE.

Which dynasty built the Kailasa temple at Ellora?

The Kailasa temple (Cave 16) at Ellora was carved under the Rashtrakuta king Krishna I in the 8th century CE. It was cut downward from a single basalt hillside and is one of the largest rock-cut monuments in the world.
